A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GISP study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original pruning experiments, including perplexity, CMQA and GSM8K accuracy, pruning time, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds medical QA, Qwen3, calibration robustness, fine-tuning and efficiency evaluations.

M1.justification: GISP retains first-order importance, normalized structural aggregation, global ranking, iterative rescoring, and perplexity or margin objectives. Algorithm 1 and Appendix A.2 provide fuller specifications without establishing a changed pruning procedure. The new LoRA experiment evaluates subsequent adaptation.

E1.justification: V2 adds MedQA medical multiple-choice evaluation and calibration in Appendix A.5. Existing language-modeling, commonsense and mathematical-reasoning coverage remains. The Qwen3 extension uses the existing GSM8K task.

E2.justification: Appendix A.4 and Table 12 add a structured adaptation of SparseLLM using Wanda-sp as its local solver. Existing baseline comparisons remain. Newly discussed GBLM, Wanda++ and Pruner-Zero are not reported as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: V2 introduces Qwen3 evaluation, post-pruning LoRA adaptation on an additional 2M CMQA samples, calibration-budget sweeps, finer sparsity evaluations, and a 60% pruning experiment. New inference profiling uses an A6000 with batch size 1 and latency, throughput and memory metrics. These extend the evaluation design while retaining the original principal experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds calibration-budget and sampling robustness studies, post-pruning adaptation, efficiency analysis, higher-sparsity testing and Qwen3 structural profiles. Figure 3(b) also extends the once-for-all analysis with individual-pruning results at 25%, 35% and 45% sparsity. Earlier iteration and objective ablations remain.

E5.justification: V1 specifies seed 0 but reports no comparable uncertainty analysis. V2 adds a separate calibration-resampling study using seeds 0–2 with mean and standard deviation, plus standard deviations across calibration budgets and a shaded trajectory plot. These new reporting practices concern calibration robustness, not all benchmark comparisons.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–6, the DeepSeek portion of Table 7, and matched appendix result tables retain their numerical entries. V2 adds substantial results for Qwen3, MedQA, SparseLLM, robustness, adaptation and efficiency. For example, new MedQA results at 20% pruning are 31.26% for GISP and 21.92% for Wanda-sp.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds exact mathematical specifications for the linear schedule and parameter-count normalization, particularly Equations 7 and 9, where v1 provided procedural descriptions. The existing Taylor expansion and objective equations remain, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of stable iterative global pruning, nested subnetworks enabling once-for-all deployment, and task-aligned importance improving downstream performance. The expanded model evidence in the abstract supports these retained contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of calibration robustness and subsequent adaptation, conjectures explaining SparseLLM's limited gains under structured pruning, and architecture-specific explanations contrasting Llama2 and Qwen3 sparsity patterns. The original limitations concerning computational cost and untested MoE architectures remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds Algorithm 1, explicit scheduling and normalization details, an official implementation link, GSM8K-specific sampling counts, inference hardware settings and quantified mask-storage requirements. It also clarifies that CMQA calibration produces one shared multitask subnetwork; this clarification does not establish a changed experiment.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion and citations for GBLM, Wanda++, Pruner-Zero and SparseLLM, distinguishing their gradient or reconstruction approaches from GISP. MedQA and Qwen3 references are also added. The existing related-work discussion is retained after relocation.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract and selected method and calibration explanations, presents the one-shot procedure as numbered steps, and moves Related Works from Section 5 to Appendix A.1. New sections are integrated while much of the existing narrative remains unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds an algorithm block, robustness and Qwen3 figures, and tables for the new comparisons and analyses. Table 7 expands to include Qwen3; Figure 3(b) gains intermediate markers and axis ticks. Existing tables are rearranged, and the original sparsity-profile Figure 4 becomes Figure 5.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important validation and documentation gaps through calibration-budget and seed studies, explicit implementation specifications, and measured inference costs. These substantially strengthen reproducibility and support for practical deployment, alongside broader comparisons. One added analysis remains ambiguous: Table 8's Wanda-sp starting scores match SparseLLM in Table 12 rather than Wanda-sp, limiting confidence in the LoRA comparison. This localized issue does not outweigh the broader gains.
